newsitem.title: FRANCE: CGIP sold Cap Gemini block.
newsitem.headline: CGIP sold Cap Gemini block.

text.p: Investment holding company CGIP has sold a block of 8.6 million shares in computer house Cap Gemini for 2.958 billion francs, bankers JP Morgan and Societe Generale said on Thursday.

The announcement in a newspaper advertisement follows CGIP's decision last month to raise its shareholding in Cap Gemini by buying a German-held stake and selling a surplus portion of it back to the market.
Cie Gnrale d'Industrie et de Participations (CGIP) said on July 9 it had raised its stake in Cap Gemini to 30 percent from 20 for a total investment of 1.86 billion francs.
It had owned first refusal on a 24 percent stake held by Daimler-Benz InterServices (DEBIS) of Germany.
CGIP said at the time it had bought the stake from DEBIS at 326 francs per share and had organised the sale of 14 percent to the market at a net price of 340 francs per share.
The operation was done through JP Morgan and Societe Generale.
